questions.evidence: At dinner, Aunt May asks whether anyone wants the last piece of cake. Leo says, 'I'm fine,' because he expects someone to offer it a second time. His cousin Nina hears a refusal and puts the cake on her own plate.
questions.explanation: Leo 期待別人再問一次，所以先客氣推辭。
options: He wants Nina to leave dinner.
He dislikes every kind of cake.
He has already eaten the last piece.
He expects another offer.

questions.prompt: Why does Nina take the cake?

questions.evidence: The next evening, Nina offers him a peach. Leo says, 'Yes, please. I would like half if you want some too.' Nina happily shares it. Neither needs to guess whether a polite phrase hides a different wish.
questions.explanation: Leo 明說想吃，也提出彼此分享。
options: He clearly accepts and suggests sharing.
He repeats 'I'm fine' and stays quiet.
He refuses because of the earlier cake.
He asks his mother to answer instead.
questions.prompt: How does Leo answer the offer of a peach?

lessons.story:
At dinner, Aunt May asks whether anyone wants the last piece of cake. Leo says, 'I'm fine,' because he expects someone to offer it a second time. His cousin Nina hears a refusal and puts the cake on her own plate.

Leo becomes quiet. Later, he tells his mother that Nina was selfish. His mother asks what Nina actually heard. Leo repeats his words and realizes that he never said he wanted the cake. In Nina's home, people usually accept the first answer.

The next evening, Nina offers him a peach. Leo says, 'Yes, please. I would like half if you want some too.' Nina happily shares it. Neither needs to guess whether a polite phrase hides a different wish.

Leo still enjoys offering food to others before serving himself. He does not decide that one family's habit is wrong. Instead, he learns to explain his wishes when different habits meet. The missing cake becomes a small lesson about asking what someone meant before judging their character.
